events.title: July 1983 riots: first large wave
events.note: Anti-Tamil violence across Sri Lanka in July 1983 is widely described as the start of large-scale flight of Tamils across the Palk Strait to Tamil Nadu.

events.title: 1990 to 1994: second wave
events.note: A second large wave of arrivals. UNHCR's series for this group in India starts in 1990, at its highest point.

events.title: Rajiv Gandhi assassinated
events.note: Former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated at Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, by an LTTE suicide bomber.

events.title: War ends
events.note: The Sri Lankan army defeated the LTTE in May 2009. UCDP records 2009 as the last year of this armed conflict.

events.title: Citizenship (Amendment) Act passed
events.note: India's Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 gives a faster path to citizenship to some non-Muslim migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan. Sri Lankan Tamil refugees are not covered.

limitations.text: India has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention
limitations.detail: India has no national refugee law. Sri Lankan refugees are registered and assisted by the Government of India rather than by UNHCR, so figures for this group come largely from the government.
limitations.to_check: Confirm both sentences against Valatheeswaran & Rajan (2011) and add the page number.

limitations.text: Camp and non-camp refugees are not separated
limitations.detail: UNHCR gives one total; the Government of India counts camp residents and registered non-camp refugees separately.

limitations.text: The Government of India total covers Tamil Nadu only
limitations.detail: The Rajya Sabha answer of 4 May 2016 also lists refugees in one camp in Odisha. The total shown here adds the Tamil Nadu camp figure and the refugees registered outside camps; it does not include Odisha.

limitations.text: The two sources count on different dates
limitations.detail: UNHCR counts on 31 December. The Government of India figure is 'as on 1 January 2016', so UNHCR's end-2015 figure is the closest in time.
UNHCR files every person in this group under 'age unknown' (2025).

limitations.text: Gender known for part of this group
limitations.detail: UNHCR gives women and men for {p0} of refugees in 2025; the rest are not split.
The figure went from {n0} to {n1} in one year. The source data doesn't say why; a change in counting can look like real movement.
Each year the figure moves by less than 3%. Steady figures can come from registers that are updated rather than recounted; the sources don't say which.
Every year shows 0, which in UNHCR's data can mean 0 or not reported.
UNHCR and IDMC both count people displaced inside the country, in different ways. They are shown side by side and never added.

sex.text: UNHCR knows the sex of {n0} of {n1} refugees ({p0}): {n2} women and {n3} men. For the other {n4} ({p1}) it doesn't say.

age.text: UNHCR gives no ages for this group: all {n0} are recorded as 'age unknown'. The data can't tell you how many are children or older people.

notes.text: Don't apply the women/men split to the whole group: it covers only {p0} of it.
Numbers of children or older people can't be given from this data.
Comparisons with other groups by age or sex are unreliable while coverage is this low.

missing_items.why: no age groups are reported for this group.
UNHCR's data doesn't cover immigration detention, and we haven't found an open dataset for this group.

footnotes.fn_34aa6521: The total statelessness figure reported relates to 17,730 stateless persons of Rohingya ethnicity who are also counted as refugees or asylum-seekers from Myanmar, mainly from Rakhine State. UNHCR’s statistical reporting generally follows a methodology that reports only one legal status for each person of concern. However, due to the size of the stateless Rohingya population displaced from Myanmar, UNHCR considers it important to reflect the dual status of this population group as both displaced and stateless. This approach is being used for India for the first time in 2019.
footnotes.fn_3fede3ef: The statistics of the remaining IDPs at the end of the year, while provided by the Government authorities at the district level, are being reviewed by the central authorities. Once this review has been concluded, the statistics will be changed accordingly.
footnotes.fn_4092beb8: The total statelessness figure reported relates to 18,174 stateless persons of Rohingya ethnicity who are also counted as refugees or asylum-seekers from Myanmar, mainly from Rakhine State. UNHCR’s statistical reporting generally follows a methodology that reports only one legal status for each person of concern. However, due to the size of the stateless Rohingya population displaced from Myanmar, UNHCR considers it important to reflect the dual status of this population group as both displaced and stateless. This approach was used for India for the first time in 2019. The reported figure does not represent an estimate of the entire stateless population.
